title: Response roster optimization and status template library
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This document describes a practical, repeatable approach to: optimizing responder rosters for multi-region LLM-serving operations, maintaining a library of status/CSR message bundles, and standardizing incident cadence during real incidents and game days. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR) while keeping customer communication concise and consistent.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all production-facing incident responders for Redwood Inference: SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, and Customer Success on-call.
- Covers roster rules, shift-sizing algorithm, prioritization for multi-tenant impact, escalation thresholds, status templates for Statuspage and customer-facing emails, and a lightweight simulation plan for quarterly game days.

Key objectives
--------------
- Maintain MTTA < 2 min for P0 alerts and MTTR < 30 minutes for single-region degradations with clear triage steps.
- Ensure every incident has a named bridge operator and a primary communicator within 10 minutes.
- Provide a single source of truth for status messaging so customers receive timely, consistent updates.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Incident owner (primary): on-call SRE or runtime engineer. Responsible for technical remediation.
- Bridge operator (coord): operator role that runs the bridge, tracks timeline, and enforces update cadence.
- Customer comms lead: usually Customer Success for enterprise-impacting incidents; if absent, the bridge operator acts as temporary comms lead.
- Escalation lead: Eng manager or on-call SWAT; invoked for cross-service degradations or public incidents.

SLOs and thresholds (operational)
---------------------------------
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for Redwood API control plane; 99.9% for model-serving endpoints.
- Latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 300ms for short-text (<= 256 tokens) hosted requests under normal load.
- Error budget triggers: when monthly availability falls below 99.9% → schedule an SLO investigation and reduce non-essential release windows.
- Pager thresholds: P0 (system-wide outage, multi-region), P1 (single-region degraded throughput/latency above p95 threshold), P2 (feature regressions, customer-impacting but contained).

Roster optimization summary
--------------------------
Principles: fairness, coverage, skill alignment, and predictable handoffs. We use a weighted-round-robin with capacity constraints and skill tags to assign shifts.
Algorithm (high level):
1) Build candidate pool for each shift window (US, EMEA, APAC) with skill tags: serving-runtime, infra, customer-success, database, networking.
2) Exclude engineers in blackout windows (on PTO, focus-windows, public holiday overrides).
3) Weight candidates by recent load: base_weight = 1, add 0.25 for recent game-day participation, subtract 0.5 for >2 critical incidents in last 30 days.
4) Enforce maximum consecutive nights rule: no more than 3 night shifts in a 30-day window.
5) Backfill: if a shift is unassigned 24 hours before start, auto-notify escalation pool (oncall-batman) and require coverage acceptance within 60 minutes or trigger paid augmentation.

Shift sizing example (recommended baseline)
-----------------------------------------
| Region | Minimum on-call responders | Dedicated bridge operator | Overflow pager |
|--------|-----------------------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| US     | 2 (SRE + Serving)           | 1 (rotating)              | 1 (on-call SWAT)
| EMEA   | 1 (SRE or Serving)          | 1 (rotating)              | 1 (on-call SWAT)
| APAC   | 1 (overnight SRE/infra)     | 0.5 (shared)              | 1 (on-call SWAT)

(Represented here as preformatted table — add to roster scheduler CSV: region, start_utc, end_utc, role, pager_id.)

Scheduling constraints and tooling
----------------------------------
- Source of truth: oncall-roster.csv in the team repo (protected branch). Columns: date,start_utc,end_utc,region,primary,secondary,bridge,notes.
- Automation: a cron job (roster-checker) runs daily at 06:00 UTC to validate coverage and send Slack reminders via PagerDuty integration.
- Swap policy: engineers can trade shifts via the roster UI; swaps must be accepted by both parties and visible in oncall-roster.csv at least 2 hours before shift start.

Runbook: rapid stabilization (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge: PagerDuty alert acknowledged within 2 min. Set severity and impact in bridge title: [P0] /region /services-affected.
2) Quick evidence snapshot (2 mins): run the evidence collector snippet:
   - curl -s "https://ops-api.internal/v1/metrics?service=serving-runtime-api&window=5m" > /tmp/incident-metrics.json
   - kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
   - redis-cli -h prefix-cache-01 INFO | head -n 20
3) Containment (5–15 mins): if CPU/GPU saturation → scale down non-critical jobs and enable burst-capacity for Dedicated pools (command: ./infra/scale_dedicated.sh --pool=dedicated-gpu --delta=+2).
4) Assign actions: owner declares a 2-step plan (diagnose + temporary mitigation) and assigns tasks in the bridge Slack channel.
5) First customer update: publish a short status (see templates below) within 10 minutes.

Bridge operation checklist
--------------------------
- Create incident channel: #bridge-incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>
- Populate summary on the bridge doc template (title, services, first_evidence, initial_sla_impact)
- Start pinned timeline and update every 15 minutes for P0/P1 incidents until stable
- If customer impact is confirmed at enterprise tier, page Customer Success and prepare an email template.

Customer and Statuspage message templates
----------------------------------------
(Use these verbatim for consistency — replace bracketed tokens like {{region}})

A) Short initial Statuspage update (public) — post within 10 minutes for P1/P0:
Title: Investigating elevated latency for {{service}} in {{region}}
Body: We are investigating reports of increased latency affecting the {{service}} in {{region}}. Users may experience higher-than-normal response times. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or as new information becomes available.
Impact: Partial outage affecting a subset of requests
Components: serving-runtime-api ({{region}})
ETA: Next update by {{time_iso}}

B) Enterprise customer short email (internal template) — send within 30 minutes when customer-impacting:
Subject: Incident: elevated latency impacting Redwood API in {{region}}
Hello {{customer_name}},
We’re currently investigating an issue causing increased latency for some requests to the Redwood API in {{region}}. Our on-call team has identified the affected component (serving-runtime-api) and is working on a mitigation. We will update you in 30 minutes or sooner.
Best,
Redwood Incident Response Team

C) Escalation-ready status update (public) — if a P0 persists >30 minutes:
Title: Service degradation — extended investigation for {{service}}
Body: Our incident response team is performing an extended investigation into a widespread service degradation. Customers may see errors or timeouts. We have opened a prioritized escalation to engineering leadership and are standing up cross-functional support. Next update in 15 minutes.

Customer comms best practices
-----------------------------
- Keep messages short, factual, and time-boxed. Avoid speculation.
- Use the same incident identifier in all comms (bridge name).
- Coordinate with Customer Success for enterprise-targeted messaging; default public updates go to Statuspage.
- Preserve audit trail: paste all customer-facing messages into the incident timeline.

Post-incident: lightweight postmortem template
---------------------------------------------
(Complete within 72 hours for P0/P1 incidents.)
1) Summary: one-paragraph timeline and impact statement.
2) What happened: short bullet list of technical root cause(s).
3) Evidence: links to logs, runbook steps executed, and key metrics (p95, error-rate).
4) Corrective actions (owners + ETA): list of action items, priority, and owner.
5) Preventative actions: deployable items (e.g., better autoscaling policy, synthetic checks).
6) Follow-up: schedule a 1-hour readout with stakeholders within 7 business days.

Quarterly game day: roster + bridge stress test
-----------------------------------------------
Purpose: exercise the roster algorithm, validate handoffs, and rehearse customer messaging under stress.
Game day structure (4 hours):
- 00:00–00:30: orientation & objectives; verify oncall-roster.csv is up-to-date.
- 00:30–01:30: scenario A — KV cache eviction cascade; goal: restore prefix-cache within 45 minutes.
- 01:30–02:30: scenario B — multi-region model-serving degradation; goal: validate automatic fallback policies and runbook steps.
- 02:30–03:30: scenario C — complicated incident: false-positive SLO breach from synthetic check; goal: rapid identification and rollback of erroneous alerting rule.
- 03:30–04:00: retro & scoring: evaluate roster fairness metrics, swap latency, and customer message timeliness.
Scoring matrix (pass/fail thresholds):
- Acknowledge < 2 minutes = pass
- Bridge up with primary = pass
- First public update < 10 minutes = pass
- Postmortem draft within 72 hours = pass

Evidence and logging standards
-----------------------------
- Always attach the evidence bundle to the incident: incident-metrics.json, pod manifests, key logs, and the event timeline.
- Retention: keep incident artifacts for 13 months for audit and SRE learning. Store in /incidents/YYYY/MM/ID on the internal S3.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets and links
--------------------------------------
- Evidence collector (one-liner): curl -sf "https://ops-api.internal/v1/collector?service=serving-runtime-api&since=5m" | jq . > /tmp/incident-$(date +%s).json
- Scale dedicated pool (ops CLI): ./opsctl scale-pool --pool dedicated-gpu --region {{region}} --increment 2
- Slack bridge command examples: /incident create title="[P1] serving-runtime-api {{region}}" owner=@pager
- Relevant pages: https://confluence.internal/redwood/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025; https://confluence.internal/redwood/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-chain-and-forensic-runbook-2025

Revision history and governance
------------------------------
- This doc lives in the oncall space and is reviewed semi-annually by the SRE and Platform leads. Significant process changes (roster algorithm, escalation thresholds) require approval from the Eng Ops council.

End of document
